basis: Migne prints his own reference to Genesis 47:31 inside this answer, which asks 'Inter. 277. Quid est quod Jacob conversus ad caput lectuli sui oravit Dominum (Gen.'. The extent is that reference and nothing wider.
date_basis: The dedicatory letter addresses Sigewulf, Alcuin's pupil and his successor at Tours, and says the questions are ones Sigewulf had put to him over a long acquaintance and are now gathered. Alcuin was abbot of Tours from 796 until his death in 804. The work is conventionally placed in the Tours years and near their beginning; the range records that and no more. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1851 printing, and it is not the seventh century the wiki header gives, which is a century out.
text: Inter. 277. Quid est quod Jacob conversus ad caput lectuli sui oravit Dominum (Gen. XLVII, 31)?-- Resp. Scilicet postquam juraverat ei filius [securus] de petitione quam rogaverat, adoravit Deum [ Ms., Dominum coepit adorare] contra caput lectuli sui; sanctus quippe et Deo obediens [ Ms., deditus] vir, oppressus senectute, habebat lectulum ita positum, ut ipse jacens [habitus] absque ulla difficultate ad orationem esset paratus.
